utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it generally known that the Presidency now consisted of five members?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to explain a moment ago that the notion of Presidency appeared when Mr. Karadzic joined Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Koljevic to make up the three-member Presidency. So in our minds, in everybody's minds, Presidency meant primarily the three of them. As for those two members who were later attached, I can say that Djeric did not feel like a member of the Presidency. He just attended meetings with them not really thinking of it as a meeting of the extended Presidency. I can't recall now that this expanded Presidency was ever some sort of separate authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not my question. My question was whether it was generally known that the Presidency on from a certain moment existed -- consisted of five persons including Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Djeric and not of three anymore.

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain that this is not something that had any practical consequences from the public point of view. I am trying to view this through the person of Mr. Djeric who was formerly a member of that expanded Presidency, he didn't think there was an expanded Presidency. There was a Presidency consisting of Mr. Karadzic, Mrs. Plavsic, and Mr. Koljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now for Mr. Krajisnik. You said Mr. Djeric didn't consider himself to be a member of the expanded Presidency. Was the same true of Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know his personal view of that body, I never heard him refer to the expanded Presidency or voice any doubts about it or suspicions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say "I did not ever hear him voice any doubts or suspicions," would that include both the existence of the five-member Presidency and his position in it or any of these subjects separate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what he thought about this expanded Presidency, not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He never said anything to you. Did he ever make any public statement in which he denied his own position in the expanded Presidency -- or I should say in which he denied his position as a member of the expanded Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about this idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have one question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not finished yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honour. I had impression - my mistake - that you were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one more question on a question by Mr. Stewart. You answered that Mr. Krajisnik did never express any concern about demographics, concerns about the number of Muslims growing. This Chamber has received at least some evidence that such concerns did exist. Are you aware of any, whether public or private, statement of Mr. Krajisnik in which he took distance from such concerns?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my next question, this Chamber has received evidence that on the 24th of May, 1992, the Presidency gave -- and now I quote, "Instructions for organisation and work of presidencies in municipalities in conditions of the imminent threat of war and a state of war," in which it was clarified that the War Presidencies had, and I quote again, "To organise, coordinate and synchronise activities for the Defence of the Serbian people and to establish governmental power." Did the government ever receive reports from Crisis Staffs or War Presidencies or War Commissions on these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Crisis Staff reports about the situation on the ground, about the functioning of the government or restoration of this functioning, were not submitted to the government. We always tried to go out into the field to gather information which was rather difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that you were seeking information rather than receiving reports from these Crisis Staffs, War Presidencies or War Commissions.

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My last question would be the following: In the November 1991 plebescite, were Serbs allowed to vote only or were other ethnicities allowed to vote as well.

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Others were allowed to vote as well. The colour of the ballots were different but others were allowed to vote as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for those answers. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Trbojevic, did Mr. Krajisnik ever make any public statement in which he confirmed his own position in the expanded Presidency, or I should say in which he confirmed his position as a member of the expanded Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MILAN TRBOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard him make any statement referring to that particular function.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Trbojevic, since there are no further questions for you, I'd like to thank you not only for coming to The Hague but for coming even two times to The Hague and for answering I now can say all the questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again. Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Trbojevic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, any news from Ms. Loukas?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, I did manage to speak to her at the beginning of the last break. Your Honour, the position is that Ms. Loukas had, in the light of yesterday, she had completely assumed that this witness would not be called today. She had diverted her work and energies elsewhere, Your Honour, and in the circumstances, it -- well, I felt in the light of her response, Your Honour, it wasn't reasonable, with respect, to expect her to come and deal with the witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that Mr. Tieger that we would adjourn but let's first see whether we can deal with any further exhibits and let's also see whether there are any further procedural matters which we should deal with. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. First of all, the exhibits. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There are three Prosecution Exhibits, P583, P583A, and P583B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. These are the statements and the audio. Since there are no objections, they are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few other procedural matters. First of all, the schedule has been changed slightly in that we moved from next Tuesday the 19th of April from the afternoon into the morning hours. That has been announced to the parties, I take it, at least the parties have been asked whether it would create any insurmountable problems. Next Tuesday, Mr. Stewart --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't think it's a problem, it is news, but I don't think it is a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Ms. Loukas has been informed about it but.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I think the problem is Your Honour because we had this hitch with the transcript. I just haven't as I normally would have done picked up these bits and pieces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not a problem. Can I just be clear, the -- Your Honour says from next Tuesday so does that mean it's mornings all week, is that the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no, then I was not -- I was unclear. I think I started saying moved from the afternoon and then I suddenly realised that the day was not clear and that therefore I switched to Tuesday and then continued from the afternoon into the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So is the position this, it's mornings Monday and Tuesday, afternoon Wednesday and Thursday, and then morning on Friday; is that the position, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well Your Honour, that's absolutely no problem at all for the Defence, may I say straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Prosecution, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm certainly not aware of any difficulty, Your Honour, but I will know as soon as we leave Court and if there is any significant problem ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I instructed one of the members of the staff of Chambers to inform the parties -- to inquire with the parties as soon as possible whether there would be any problem. I didn't hear anything else so therefore it's now a formal announcement that we'll sit next Tuesday in the morning. Then Mr. Stewart, yesterday, in relation to -- in relation to protective measures for witnesses to come, some of them testifying about sexual abuse, the Defence was invited to see whether they would agree with the request made by the Prosecution and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in fact, I was invited yesterday specifically in relation to just one of those witnesses in a sense that of course I -- I think I was being invited at some point of course to consider them all, but yesterday, the discussion was specifically related just to one where I understood there was a degree of urgency and I did deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think it was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can only report the communications that I received from the Prosecution, Your Honour, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, but yesterday I addressed the matter in Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was telephoned at home by the Prosecution towards the end of the morning and I dealt with specifically the request that I was asked to deal with yesterday as it was reported to me. That's all I can say I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think a few matters might have been mixed up. Yesterday I made an observation to more witnesses which I addressed mainly the matter that, under the case law of this Tribunal, victims of sexual abuse usually would be granted private session for at least those parts relating to that sexual abuse. The Prosecution ever asked for -- in more respects for private session and I inquired whether the Defence would consider to agree to that. At the same time, and during that part of yesterday's session, we were informed that for one of these witnesses, that in addition to the protective measures sought in the motion, that the witness had expressed a wish to testify in closed session, I think. So therefore, there might be some confusion as to the addition to the original motion which was not primarily addressed by me but which then came up during the session and as a reaction to the observations I've made at that time but I think it was Mr. Hannis who added this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour then if I can tell Your Honour exactly what happened. I was contacted, I think it was around half past 12.00 or something like that, I was contacted by the Prosecution. They raised specifically that last point in relation to that one witness and invited me to respond as a matter of urgency. I spoke to Mr. Gaynor who sent me an e-mail and I did respond as a matter of urgency. I think, Your Honour, I'm not a hundred per cent sure, I think at some point then I said to Ms. Loukas something like, later on after she came out of court, something like, "I'm dealing with a protective witness's issue but you needn't worry about that today because I'm dealing with it." That's as far as it went. I didn't understand that there was any more urgent issue yesterday than the one raised in relation to that single witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said yesterday if the Defence would consider, that might save some further efforts if there would be an agreement on especially these three witnesses, I think it was, that we'd like to know as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well Your Honours can know as soon as possible in relation to the other two, now it's been indicated to me that the answer is needed very soon because I had understood yesterday that the only matter -- after all, I did have one or two other things to do, Your Honour, I had understood yesterday that the only matter requiring my immediate attention, which I gave it, was in relation to that one witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, I invited the Defence yesterday to express itself on the three witnesses but let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm sure you that invitation didn't get through to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I'm not insisting on anything. We identified where the confusion might have -- might find its source. If the Chamber could hear about this -- whether the Defence, having considered what we yesterday raised would lead to agree with the proposal, we'd like to know. If not, then of course we expect a response as normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I was being too impatient with my response. Your Honour, I was simply going to say on that one witness, after all, I don't -- naturally we can say this openly because we're only saying "that witness" on that witness there, there is a supplemental information, I did indicate that the Defence would have no opposition to the relief sought in the original motion but did not agree with the additional protection sought in that supplement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So Your Honour, I didn't specifically consider the other two witnesses but I'm sure Your Honour can see that that's unlikely to take me long to do in the course of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not do it at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In the course of this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what is in dispute in relation to that third witness is whether the additional protective measures sought should be granted, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just add this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I did expressly say in my e-mail response which was done very urgently in the middle of a very heavy day on other matters, I did say that that did not constitute the Defence response. I was -- the Prosecution did particularly wanted me to give an indication immediately as to my position, so I did say I agree to the motion as originally sought, I did just indicate -- I did not agree to the supplemental, but I did expressly say that was not a formal Defence response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. The Chamber would like to know as soon as possible to what extent the Defence agrees with the protective measures sought and to the extent you do not agree, we'll hear from you in the way as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, that's now very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In light of the circumstances at least as I them, "as soon as possible" takes on perhaps a slightly more constricted and urgent meaning and I think ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say I'm not fully aware at this moment -- one of these witnesses was scheduled for relatively early next week. I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that's right, Your Honour well, one thing is clear, a further decision cannot be any further delayed than when the witness arrives, of course, unless you also delay the arrival of the witness. Mr. Stewart, could you let us know -- could you tell me when you expect to be able to give the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll do it this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's -- well, I take it that Mr. Tieger is quite happy with -- that as soon as possible would be this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, and again, my objective is, if possible, to reach a resolution of this issue today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In light of the -- our early recess today, I would hope we could all work together to make that happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber cannot do anything else than to see whether there's any agreement between the parties. If there's no agreement, what the arguments of the parties are and then to take a decision. The Chamber is, to the extent that we are all there, because we have not, of course not only this case, the only thing we can do is the sooner you come with your information, the sooner even informally sometimes, of course, if the Chamber reaches a decision, the parties can be informed about what the decision is even without knowing already all the reasons of it which will then be pronounced at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's at all helpful, I said this afternoon. I would do it by 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm still available after 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I will do it by 4.00, Your Honour, that's my -- I don't say it's my final offer, Your Honour, it's my offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if it could possibly be done earlier, we would appreciate that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, may I simply raise this. Mr. Krajisnik has asked me and it's entirely reasonable request, Your Honour. Mr. Krajisnik would like to know if there are any days in the reasonably near future, apart from the 29th of April, which we know about as the Dutch Queen's Day when the Trial Chamber would not or might not be sitting because he is trying to arrange some visits by his family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware of one day of court schedule but I do not know ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any confusion that we are not only not sitting on the 29th but not the whole week after that as well? I think that was communicated to the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour is indicating that we are not sitting that following week; is that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Actually, if that, again, it's not totally impossible that communications don't always end up with me, but I wasn't ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to me we're not only not sitting that Friday, the 29th, but also not sitting the week following that Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Your Honour, that's most helpful to know. If -- well, it doesn't matter, Your Honour, whether I knew before. I did know that I was going to ask because I did know that a week not sitting in May was contemplated but my brain hadn't absorbed at some point what week it was. That's most helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there is another day of court maintenance where we are not sitting ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm now informed that that would be the 13th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour this is all extremely helpful for planning, of course, so thank you very much for that and I'm sure it would be helpful to Mr. Krajisnik as well, particularly, the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further issues? Then I've got one tiny little thing to say about something that happened in the beginning of this -- today's session. Mr. Stewart, you introduced a question to Mr. Trbojevic in which you perfectly in accordance with the statement of the witness, you said something about why Mr. Margetts did not hear any further information about because he knew everything, et cetera, et cetera. That of course triggered a kind of a defence action for Mr. Margetts. I think Defence action was not necessary just as the detailed information on why Mr. Margetts, during that interview, stopped Mr. Trbojevic did not add anything to the question put to Mr. Trbojevic and was quite suitable for triggering -- you understand what I mean. If you would have asked Mr. Trbojevic, you started answering that question during -- you were stopped by Mr. Margetts, could you please now give us the information you at that moment could not give. That would have been totally sufficient, that would triggered any defence action here and it certainly would have contributed to make the relationship between the parties even more excellent as it is already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just say on that, Your Honour, I hear exactly what Your Honour says and register that. I hope it's appreciated that every word I said about Mr. Margetts's reasons came from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes I have no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's just that I didn't add any gratuitous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I said, it didn't add anything to the issue you wanted to raise with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I understand. I understand Your Honour's point. No, I just got the feeling that perhaps it might be -- might have been heard by others from what Your Honour said that I had gratuitously added some comments, which I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I understand what Your Honour says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I literally followed it and it was quite suitable to trigger what happened then which, as I said, did not contribute to even improving the already excellent relationship between it's parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well Your Honour I've spoken to Mr. Margetts since, so I think we're still on speaking terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn until next Monday, 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of April, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.12 p.m.
